questions.question:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.

He comes here _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adverb **"daily"** is used to indicate something that happens every day.
 
• In the context of the sentence, "He comes here _________," the most appropriate adverb to use is "daily" because it makes sense that someone comes to a place every day.
 
• The other options do not fit the context as well as** "daily."**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"He comes here **daily**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "lately" **– This means recently and does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "quickly"** – This describes the speed of the action, not the frequency, so it is not appropriate here.
 
• **Option 3: "formerly"** – This means in the past and does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 5: (blank)** – This is not a valid option as it provides no adverb to complete the sentence.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

That day we reached late for the competition and even though the competition went on smooth, I felt bad about Shivani losing it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "the competition went on smooth" is incorrect.
 
• The word "smooth" should be replaced with the adverb "smoothly" to describe how the competition went on.
 
• Adverbs are used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, and in this context, "smoothly" correctly modifies the verb "went on".
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"That day we reached late for the competition and even though the competition went on smoothly, I felt bad about Shivani losing it."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "I felt bad" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "losing it"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "we reached late"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
The sentence below contains errors. Select the option with the correct use of tenses.

I will revised my course at least three times before my final examination.

options.text: I will have revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
I must revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
I would revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
I will be revised my course at least three times since my final examination.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb tense.
 
• The phrase "I will revised" is grammatically incorrect because "revised" is the past form and cannot be used with "will."
 
• The correct future perfect tense is "I will have revised."
 
• This indicates that the action of revising will be completed before the final examination.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"I will have revised my course at least three times before my final examination."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "I must revised" is incorrect; "must" should be followed by the base form of the verb "revise."
 
• **Option 3:** "I would revised" is incorrect; "would" should be followed by the base form of the verb "revise."
 
• **Option 4:** "I will be revised" is incorrect; "will be" should be followed by a present participle (revising) not past participle (revised).

questions.question:
Choose an appropriate word that can substitute the bracketed word and complete the sentence meaningfully.

What is the time (in) your watch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition** "in" **is often used to indicate location or time within something, but in the context of a watch, "by" is the correct preposition to use.
 
• **"By"** is used to indicate the means or instrument used to measure or indicate something, in this case, time.
 
• The correct phrase is "What is the time by your watch?" which is commonly used to ask for the time indicated on someone's watch.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"What is the time **by** your watch?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **on** – This preposition is used to indicate a surface or a day/date, and is incorrect in this context.
 
• **with** – This preposition implies possession or accompaniment and is incorrect in this context.
 
• **into** – This preposition indicates movement towards the inside of something and is incorrect in this context.
